prediction.raw: 0 I think your actions are wrong. While your intention to feed the endangered species and prevent it from dying may have been good, taking it from its natural habitat and killing it to make it into taxidermy is not a justifiable or ethical solution. Endangered species are protected by laws and international agreements for a reason, and removing them from their habitat can disrupt the ecosystem and further threaten their survival. Additionally, taxidermy does not provide any conservation benefits and can even perpetuate harmful attitudes towards wildlife. A more appropriate course of action would have been to contact local wildlife authorities or conservation organizations for guidance on how to help the animal without causing harm. They could have provided assistance, such as transporting the animal to a rehabilitation center or providing advice on how to safely feed and care for it in its natural habitat.
